scoring_justification: Hot spot peak frequency checked against paper reference (-0.3 eV); cold spot peak proximity checked; full recompute of Green's function recursion is infeasible in checker. NMR crossover verified via structural trend (derivative sign change at T_cr).

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold reference for spectral peak positions and crossover temperature
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Fig. 1: hot quasiparticle high-energy feature ~ -0.3 eV; cold quasiparticle peak near zero. Paper text: T_cr=470 K, crossover in chi_Q^2/gamma_Q.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Derived from paper's reported results; used as hidden comparison values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values correspond to the paper's published experiment; not invented for this task.

outputs.description: Spectral density A(k,ω) on the Fermi surface for hot (kx=1.0,ky=0.0) and cold (kx=0.5,ky~0.5) quasiparticles at ξ=3, T=500 K. The hidden checker locates the maximum spectral density for ω<0 at the hot spot and verifies its frequency within a tolerance, and checks that the cold spot maximum lies near zero.

Temperature dependence of spin damping γ_Q and the product χ_Q²/γ_Q (proportional to ⁶³T₁T/(⁶³T₂G)²). The hidden checker computes the numerical derivative of ratio_chiQ2_over_gammaQ with respect to temperature and verifies it is positive for T<470 K and non-positive for T>470 K, confirming the crossover.

output_contract.notes: All model parameters (t, t', g, ξ(T) forms) are extracted from the source paper. Only standard scientific Python libraries are required; no proprietary software or external datasets needed. The agent must perform the full numerical evaluation of the recursion relations.
